keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row; its Duchy of Racibórz row covers 1285-1304 and the Kingdom of Poland shapes draw the area later). 'It was established about 1315 on the Lesser Polish lands east of the Biała river'. The page gives no area; at the 1457 sale it lists two towns (Oświęcim and Kęty), two ducal castles and 45 villages.
'In 1445 the duchies of Zator and Toszek were created from some the lands of the duchy.'

region.text: the Lesser Polish lands east of the Biała river, with the lands from which Zator and Toszek were created in 1445

ledger.note: c. 1315: Oświęcim splits from Cieszyn. 'It was established about 1315 on the Lesser Polish lands east of the Biała river'; 'the lands of Oświęcim east of the Biała were split off from [Cieszyn] as a separate duchy' (the Teschen page: 'Oświęcim split off around 1315').

region.text: the duchies of Zator and Toszek, created from some of the lands in 1445

ledger.note: 1445: 'the duchies of Zator and Toszek were created from some the lands of the duchy'. The page names no boundary; the two radii are my reading.

1457: the last duke, Jan IV, 'sold his duchy to King Casimir for the price of 3,000,000 Prague groschen' three years after declaring himself a vassal of Poland in 1454 ('re-united with Poland in 1454'). The sale list: two towns (Oświęcim and Kęty), two castles, 45 villages.
1457: the Duchy of Oświęcim ends; 'At the General sejm of 1564, King Sigismund II Augustus issued privileges of incorporation' into the Kraków Voivodeship.

certainty.note: The page names towns and the Biała river, not a boundary.

notes:
The Duchy of Oświęcim is a state Cliopatria lacks (eu-15-i flagged the Cieszyn family). The Bohemian vassalage (1327, Jan I the Scholastic's homage to John of Bohemia) and the Polish vassalage declared by Jan IV in 1454 are the overlords' ledgers: kingdom-of-bohemia should carry vassal_start 1327 (vassal_end 1454/1457) and kingdom-of-poland vassal_start 1454, naming duchy-of-oswiecim.

Not settled: (1) The duchies of Zator and Toszek (1445) have no dossier; the Toszek radius is a guess (the page names no location). (2) The Oświęcim page gives no area; the Cieszyn radii are stand-ins. (3) No ruler list or wars on the page. (4) 'about 1315' is approximate, hence confidence 2.
